title_en: Taifeng Hotel Co., Ltd. v. Datong City Land Administration Bureau — dispute over land use right grant
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over assignment of land use rights; second instance; High People's Court; Shanxi Province; legal person; state organ; Interim Regulations on the Assignment and Transfer of the Right to Use State-Owned Land in Urban Areas; General Principles of Civil Law; application of the rule on earnest money penalties; whether the assignment fee for land use rights should be refunded; whether the statute of limitations is interrupted; partially upheld; contract for assignment of land use rights; overdue payment; rescission of contract; confiscation of earnest money and assignment fee; good faith; land use rights; statute of limitations; Administration Bureau's dispute over assignment of land use rights
full_text_en:
Taifeng Grand Hotel Co., Ltd. v. Datong City Land Administration Bureau — Dispute over Land Use Rights Grant

Plaintiff: Shanxi Taifeng Grand Hotel Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Meng Baoyun, Chairman

Agent ad litem: Zhao Jinrong, lawyer of the Third Law Firm of Datong City, Shanxi Province

Defendant: Datong City Land Administration Bureau of Shanxi Province

Legal Representative: Mu Fuxiang, Director

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shijie, official of the Datong City Land Administration Bureau of Shanxi Province

The plaintiff, Shanxi Taifeng Grand Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taifeng Company), filed a lawsuit with the Datong Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province against the defendant, Datong City Land Administration Bureau of Shanxi Province (hereinafter referred to as the Land Bureau), over a dispute concerning the grant of the right to use state-owned land.

The plaintiff alleged: After the defendant unilaterally tore up the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" voluntarily signed with the plaintiff, it not only refused to return the deposit paid by the plaintiff, but also confiscated the land use rights grant fee paid by the plaintiff. Despite repeated negotiations by the plaintiff, the defendant refused to return the money. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to return the land use rights grant fee of RMB 2,793,131.05 paid by the plaintiff, and to compensate for the bank interest accrued during the period of occupation of this sum, or to order the defendant to continue to perform the land use rights grant contract.

The defendant argued: After the plaintiff paid the deposit and part of the land use rights grant fee, the remaining amount was not paid as agreed despite repeated reminders by the defendant, and the plaintiff still owes liquidated damages of over RMB 7.9 million, causing losses to the defendant. Therefore, according to the contract, the defendant decided to terminate the contract and, pursuant to Article 14 of the Interim Regulations on the Grant and Transfer of the Right to Use State-owned Land in Cities and Towns of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations) and Article 11 of the Shanxi Province Implementation Measures for the Grant and Transfer of the Right to Use State-owned Land in Cities and Towns (hereinafter referred to as the Shanxi Implementation Measures), decided not to return the deposit and land use rights grant fee already paid by the plaintiff, to compensate for the losses caused to the defendant. The plaintiff's filing of this lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations, and the people's court should dismiss the claim according to law.

After trial, the Datong Intermediate People's Court found: On November 23, 1993, the plaintiff, Taifeng Company (Party B of the contract), and the defendant, the Land Bureau (Party A of the contract), in accordance with the provisions of the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations, through negotiation and mutual agreement, voluntarily signed the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract." The contract stipulated: Party A would grant the right to use 8,939.77 square meters of state-owned land located at the northwest corner of Gulou, Chengqu District, Datong City, to Party B for commercial construction for a period of 40 years, with a land use rights grant fee of RMB 8,045,793. Within 30 days after the signing of the contract, Party B would first pay 15% of the total land use rights grant fee (amounting to RMB 1,206,868.95) to Party A as a contract deposit, and pay the full land use rights grant fee within 60 days. If Party B failed to pay the full land use rights grant fee within an additional 30 days, Party A had the right to terminate the contract and claim compensation. Within 5 days after Party B paid the full land use rights grant fee, the procedures for registering the land use rights would be carried out according to regulations, and the "State-owned Land Use Certificate of the People's Republic of China" would be obtained, thereby acquiring the land use rights.

After the contract was signed, on December 27, 1993, the plaintiff, Taifeng Company, paid RMB 4,000,000 to the defendant, the Land Bureau. This amount included the contract deposit of RMB 1,206,868.95 and the land use rights grant fee of RMB 2,793,131.05. Taifeng Company also submitted a written application to the Land Bureau, stating that due to cash flow difficulties and the inability to construct in winter, it requested a postponement of the unpaid land use rights grant fee until April 1, 1994. The Land Bureau agreed to Taifeng Company's application and, on December 28, 1993, issued to Taifeng Company a state-owned land use certificate for 8,939.77 square meters bearing the seals of "Datong City People's Government" and "Datong City Land Administration Bureau." However, Taifeng Company did not pay the outstanding land use rights grant fee by April 1, 1994. Despite repeated reminders by the Land Bureau, Taifeng Company still failed to perform. On September 22, 1994, the Land Bureau issued a written notice to Taifeng Company, requiring it to fulfill all payment obligations by September 30, or it would be dealt with according to relevant regulations. After receiving the written notice, Taifeng Company orally promised the Land Bureau to fulfill all obligations by the end of September, but again failed to do so by the deadline. The Land Bureau, pursuant to Article 14 of the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations, which provides: "The land user shall pay the full land use rights grant fee within 60 days after signing the land use rights grant contract. If the full payment is not made within the time limit, the grantor has the right to terminate the contract and may claim compensation for breach of contract," and Article 11 of the Shanxi Implementation Measures, which provides: "If the grantee fails to perform the contract, the grantor may terminate the contract according to law, and the deposit and grant fee paid shall not be returned," decided on September 30, 1994: to terminate the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed with Taifeng Company on November 23, 1993, to reclaim the land use rights within the scope stipulated in the contract, to cancel and deregister the land use certificate issued, and not to return the deposit of RMB 1,206,868.95 and the land use rights grant fee of RMB 2,793,131.05 already paid by Taifeng Company. On October 24, 1994, after receiving the notice of the decision to terminate the contract, Taifeng Company negotiated with the Land Bureau multiple times and, in March and April of 1996, reported to the Datong City People's Government requesting a resolution, but all were fruitless. Taifeng Company then filed this lawsuit on August 20, 1997.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the state-owned land use rights grant contract signed by the plaintiff and defendant, payment receipts, the state-owned land use certificate, the notice of termination of the contract, Taifeng Company's report to the Datong City People's Government, and the record of statements of the parties. This evidence, having been cross-examined, can serve as the basis for establishing the facts.

The Datong Intermediate People's Court held: Article 11 of the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations stipulates: "The land use rights grant contract shall be signed between the land administration department of the city or county people's government (hereinafter referred to as the grantor) and the land user on the principles of equality, voluntariness, and compensation." This shows that between the grantor and the grantee in a land use rights grant contract, there is a relationship of equality in civil matters. The land use rights grant contract signed between the defendant, the Land Bureau, and the plaintiff, Taifeng Company, conforms to the principles of equality, voluntariness, and exchange of equivalent values, and is valid. Article 89 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides that parties may use methods such as guarantees, mortgages, deposits, etc., to secure the performance of a contract in accordance with legal provisions or the agreement of the parties. The agreement between the Land Bureau and Taifeng Company in the land use rights grant contract to use 15% of the total land use rights grant fee as a contract deposit is valid and is legally binding on both parties. Article 89(3) of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "A party may pay a deposit to the other party within the scope provided by law. After the debtor performs its obligations, the deposit shall be credited against the price or returned. If the party paying the deposit fails to perform its obligations, it has no right to demand the return of the deposit; if the party receiving the deposit fails to perform its obligations, it shall return the deposit in double." Taifeng Company's failure to pay the full land use rights grant fee within the period stipulated in the contract constitutes a failure to perform the contractual obligations, and it has no right to demand the return of the deposit. As for the portion of the land use rights grant fee already paid by Taifeng Company, the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations do not contain a provision for "no return," and the Land Bureau's confiscation of these funds is without legal basis. Taifeng Company's claim for compensation from the Land Bureau for bank interest during the period of occupation of these funds is not supported, because Taifeng Company was in breach of contract first. The Land Bureau's refusal to return the contract deposit, which was legally based on Taifeng Company's breach, serves both to penalize Taifeng Company's breach and to compensate for the Land Bureau's losses. The Land Bureau failed to provide evidence proving that its losses exceeded the contract deposit it received, so its argument that it did not return the land use rights grant fee to compensate for the losses caused by Taifeng Company is untenable. Regarding the Land Bureau's argument that Taifeng Company's lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations, the evidence provided by Taifeng Company shows that in March and April of 1996, Taifeng Company had asserted its rights in a report submitted to the Datong City Government, which should be deemed as an interruption of the statute of limitations. Accordingly, on November 27, 1997, the Datong Intermediate People's Court ruled:

Within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, the defendant, the Land Bureau, shall refund to the plaintiff, Taifeng Company, the land use rights grant fee of RMB 2,793,131.05.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance of RMB 35,963 shall be borne by the defendant, the Land Bureau.

After the first instance judgment was announced, the defendant, the Land Bureau, refused to accept it and appealed to the Shanxi High People's Court, requesting a reversal. The reasons were: 1. The contract signed between the appellant, the Land Bureau, and the appellee, Taifeng Company, was fully executed in accordance with the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations and the Shanxi Implementation Measures. The land use rights grant fee of RMB 2,793,131.05 paid by Taifeng Company was not confiscated by the Bureau but was dealt with as non-refundable under Article 11 of the Shanxi Implementation Measures. Although Article 14 of the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations does not specify non-refundability, it also does not specify that it should be refunded. 2. After Taifeng Company received the appellant's notice of termination of the contract on October 24, 1994, for nearly three years, it only repeatedly requested to re-accept the land and never claimed the return of the land use rights grant fee. This claim was only raised when it filed the lawsuit in August 1997, which is far beyond the statute of limitations provided in the General Principles of the Civil Law. Moreover, the Land Bureau, in signing the land use rights grant contract, was a civil subject equal to Taifeng Company. Taifeng Company should have asserted its rights to the Land Bureau or the people's court; asserting its rights to others cannot interrupt the statute of limitations. The first instance judgment's vague statement that "the plaintiff asserted its rights" to cover up Taifeng Company's lawsuit exceeding the statute of limitations is erroneous.

After trial, the Shanxi High People's Court held that the facts found by the first instance judgment were clear and the evidence was reliable and sufficient. Article 14 of the Grant and Transfer Interim Regulations does not contain a provision that the grant fee is non-refundable. Article 53 of the same Regulations provides: "These Regulations shall be interpreted by the State Land Administration Bureau." Therefore, the provision for "non-refundability" in Article 11 of the Shanxi Implementation Measures, being neither authorized by administrative regulations nor inconsistent with administrative regulations, is invalid. The grantor and grantee of state-owned land use rights are civil subjects of equal status and should deal with each other based on fairness and the principle of exchange of equivalent values. The appellant, the Land Bureau, as the grantor, by not refunding the deposit it received, has already sanctioned the breach of contract by the appellee, Taifeng Company. Apart from that, Taifeng Company has caused no other damage to the Land Bureau and has obtained no benefit from the Land Bureau. The Land Bureau has no reason to continue to hold the land use rights grant fee paid by Taifeng Company. The Land Bureau's decision not to refund the land use rights grant fee paid by Taifeng Company is untenable. The Datong City People's Government is the superior authority of the Land Bureau, and the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" issued by the Land Bureau to Taifeng Company bears the seal of the "Datong City People's Government." After the dispute between Taifeng Company and the Land Bureau arose, Taifeng Company's request to the Datong City People's Government for a resolution has the same effect as directly asserting its rights to the Land Bureau. The request to re-accept the land and the request to refund the land use rights grant fee already paid are mutually exclusive. When asserting its rights, Taifeng Company could only choose one; it could not make both requests simultaneously. Therefore, Taifeng Company's request only to re-accept the land does not mean it voluntarily gave up the right to request the refund of the land use rights grant fee; once the request to re-accept the land cannot be satisfied, the refund of the land use rights grant fee becomes its necessary request. The Land Bureau's argument that Taifeng Company's request for a refund of the land use rights grant fee was only raised at the time of filing the lawsuit and has exceeded the statute of limitations is untenable. The first instance judgment correctly applied the law and the procedure was legal. Accordingly, on July 28, 1999, the Shanxi High People's Court, in accordance with Article 153(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

Appeal fee of RMB 35,963 shall be borne by the appellant, the Land Bureau.
